item.title: My current learning trajectory
item.description: State of my learning and research trajectory
item.content:encoded:
A placeholder for my current learning trajectory. I will be updating this page with my current learning and research trajectory. This is a work in progress and will be updated as I learn more.

19-09-2026

  • Googledeepmind course to train a small language model on a small dataset. This is a good starting point to understand the basics of training a language model and the challenges involved in training a large language model. The course is available at https://www.deepmind.com/learning-resources.

Inspiration for a small LM project

https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.07759 TinyStories paper studied how large a model needs to be to be coherent and impressive in english language. We can think of usecases where the corpus is not huge, maybe words and text relevant to a specific task and train a small model of 5-10M parameters. It could be interesting to understand if we can Curate text-datasets via the best models out there that helps a small model become powerful as much as possible.

Next, the following paper asks about the probability and computations of rare outputs in LLMs. This can be studied in an interesting setting. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.13211

The blockquote element represents content that is quoted from another source, optionally with a citation which must be within a footer or cite element, and optionally with in-line changes such as annotations and abbreviations.

item.title: Rich Content
item.description: A brief description of Hugo Shortcodes
item.content:encoded:
Hugo ships with several Built-in Shortcodes for rich content, along with a Privacy Config and a set of Simple Shortcodes that enable static and no-JS versions of various social media embeds.

Images

Cheat sheet for this site. Image lookup and processing live in layouts/_default/_markup/render-image.html, layouts/shortcodes/img.html and layouts/partials/image/. The full option list is in the comment at the top of layouts/shortcodes/img.html.

Where to put images

Put shared images in assets/images/. Images there can be cropped and resized at build time. Any of these path styles works, from any post:

![alt](fig.png)
![alt](images/fig.png)
![alt](/images/fig.png)
![alt](../images/fig.png)

Lookup order:

  1. the post’s own folder (when the post is a folder with an index.md)
  2. the section folder, e.g. content/posts/images/
  3. assets/ and assets/images/
  4. static/ and static/images/ (served as-is, cannot be cropped or resized; only the CSS display options work)

If an image isn’t found, hugo prints a WARN Image "..." not found line. Check the build output.

Third-party images work as usual:

Quick crop in plain markdown

Add options after a ?:

![Attractor](images/CLV1_in_XZfor_truth.png?fill=600x300&anchor=top)
![Small plot](images/4dvar-4dvarnet-plot.png?resize=400x)

Full control: the img shortcode

{{< img src="images/CLV1_in_XZfor_truth.png" fill="800x400" anchor="top"
        width="70%" align="center" caption="Covariant Lyapunov vector 1" link="true" >}}

Cropping and resizing (makes a new image file at build time; for images in assets/ or a post’s own folder; pick one):

Option Example What it does
fill fill="800x400" scale and crop to exactly 800×400 (usually what you want)
crop crop="800x400" cut an 800×400 region out of the original, no scaling
fit fit="800x400" shrink to fit inside 800×400, keep the aspect ratio
resize resize="600x", resize="x400" scale to a width and/or height

Order of precedence if several are given: fill > crop > fit > resize.

Modifiers:

Option Values Notes
anchor center (default), smart, top, bottom, left, right, topleft, topright, bottomleft, bottomright which part survives a fill/crop; smart lets Hugo pick the most detailed area
quality 1–100 JPEG/WebP quality
rotate 90, 180, 270 counter-clockwise rotation
format webp, png, jpg convert the output

Display only (CSS, original file untouched; also works for SVGs and static/ images):

Option Example What it does
width / height width="70%", width="400px" size on the page
ratio ratio="16/9", ratio="1/1" crop the visible area to this aspect ratio
position position="30% 20%" with ratio: the focus point (x% y%) that stays in view. Use this for a precise crop that anchor can’t express

Other: alt, caption (markdown allowed), title, align (left, center, right), link ("true" opens the original on click, or give a URL), class.

Recipes

<!-- Square thumbnail from the top-left corner -->
{{< img src="images/enhanced_L63_attr_12.png" fill="400x400" anchor="topleft" >}}

<!-- Shrink a huge figure so the page loads fast, keep full-res on click -->
{{< img src="images/enhanced_L63_attr_12.png" resize="1200x" link="true" >}}

<!-- Banner crop with an exact focus point (CSS) -->
{{< img src="images/CLV2_in_XZfor_truth.png" resize="1500x" ratio="21/9" position="50% 30%" >}}

<!-- Small right-aligned image with a caption -->
{{< img src="images/schematic.png" fit="300x300" align="right" caption="*Schematic*" >}}
